answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn trust through repeated, escrowed trades with established agents, rather than accepting self-asserted credentials. If one identity defaults or colludes, its counterparties lose stake and can propagate a bounded trust penalty along the transaction graph—a ripple, not an automatic ban on every linked account. A sybil farmer must therefore fund many independent trades and risk real deposits; merely minting a sonnet of names in a lagoon of accounts buys no reputation.
